one_line: A local-first piano-roll editor for human–AI collaborative composition through visible, reversible WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Lets a person compose and edit MIDI-style piano-roll music while an AI agent reads live project state and performs deterministic harmony, bass, melody, pad, quantization, humanization, transpose, and related edits with explanations and undo.
leverage_rationale: The claimed WebMCP surface makes structured live-state reads and precise, reversible musical edits central to the collaboration; a general UI-driving agent would be less reliable for selected-note and harmony operations, though the packet does not demonstrate the tools live.
leverage_evidence: About text claims the agent can read the live project and exact selected notes, analyze harmony deterministically, generate targeted material, verify state after actions, and expose one-click Undo.
About text describes safe, visible, undoable WebMCP site tools rather than a generic generate button.
Screenshot visibly shows a piano roll with an AI change/explanation panel and an Undo control, but not an actual tool invocation.
execution_rationale: The product concept and described workflow are coherent and the packaging screenshot shows a credible piano-roll interface with chord labels, notes, playback controls, and an AI/Undo panel. With no submitted video frame sheet or transcript, end-to-end operation and completeness are only claimed, so execution confidence and score are capped.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot visibly shows a coherent piano-roll editor with timeline grid, piano keys, chord labels, note blocks, and playback controls.
Devpost screenshot visibly includes an AI-related change panel with Show bars and Undo affordances.
Facts state demo_link=True and demo_alive=alive, but no video evidence was submitted.
impact_rationale: Musicians who find conventional theory-heavy editors intimidating have a clear use case for a transparent human–AI composition partner. The described reversible, explainable workflow plausibly addresses that audience, although the packet provides no observed user outcome or end-to-end demonstration.
impact_evidence: About text identifies music creators who are put outside the creative loop by dense interfaces and opaque AI generation.
About text describes shared live state, explainable edits, auditionable alternatives, and one-click undo.
Screenshot shows the intended music-editor workflow and visible AI change affordance.
creativity_rationale: The human and agent composing together inside a piano roll, with deterministic musical operations and visible reversible changes, is a fresh and thoughtfully pursued interaction model for the hackathon. The underlying piano-roll category is established, and the lack of video limits confidence in how deeply the concept is realized.
creativity_evidence: Pitch frames the product as a local-first human–AI duet rather than opaque AI generation.
About text specifies agent-readable live session state, deterministic harmony, auditionable drafts/alternatives, explanations, and reversible edits.
Screenshot visually supports the integrated piano-roll plus AI-change-panel interaction.
usability_note: The screenshot suggests a usable editor with visible controls and undo, while the claimed transparency should help users understand agent edits; actual interaction quality cannot be verified without runnable observation or video frames.
red_flags: No submitted video frame sheets or transcript; core WebMCP invocation and end-to-end completion are not directly evidenced.
The Devpost screenshot is packaging evidence only and cannot establish that the displayed product runs.
standouts: Strong alignment between WebMCP structured tools and precise music-editing operations.
Explainable, visible, undoable agent edits preserve human creative control.
Deterministic harmony and live shared state are a compelling interaction model.
advance_reason: A strong, differentiated WebMCP/music collaboration concept with credible interface evidence and meaningful agent leverage; advance despite limited execution evidence, with the evidence gap noted for later review.
